svg.title: Filtering vs Smoothing
svg.desc: Filtering estimates the state in real time from data up to t; smoothing re-estimates past states using the whole sample.
svg.text: Filtering vs smoothing — same model, different information set
Estimating now from what is known now vs rewriting the past with the full sample
Real time — the past is not
Only the latest value is updated
Lags behind and is sensitive to noise
After the fact — every past estimate
A forward pass, then a backward pass
cannot be used in real time
Uses data up to t only
Future observations do not exist yet
Looking back at the same date changes the estimate
Real-time estimates lag and the band is wide
Turning points are caught a beat late
Seen afterwards it is smooth and the band is tight
Turning points land where they belong
Filtering is the best you can do now; smoothing is the best once later information is in.
Filter for real-time decisions, smooth for retrospective reading — mixing them creates look-ahead bias.
To the filtered estimate built from past information,
obtained by multiplying in the likelihood of future data
Next: inside one filter step — predict, update and the Kalman gain.
